title: Stop surfacing raw exception .toString() text to Sacred Time users
why: LocationFetchResult already models the common failure modes (service disabled, permission denied) as clean typed variants with their own l10n strings, but the catch-all LocationFetchError carries e.toString() verbatim — including a TimeoutException after the 15s GPS timeout, a common indoor/poor-signal scenario — rendered directly via sacredTimeLocationDetectError(message). Separately, CitiesRepository never converts its SQLite/IO exceptions, so citySearchProvider's raw AsyncError is shown via e.toString() in the error branch. Both put untranslated, technical English text inside an otherwise fully-Hebrew screen. coding-standards.md names this exact defect class as recurring, citing prior fixes (ST-4, SY-3).
recommendation: Give LocationFetchError (and CitiesRepository's failure paths) a stable enum/code instead of a free-text message, resolved to a localized string in presentation; reserve e.toString() for AppLogger only, never for display.
acceptance_criteria: LocationFetchError carries a typed reason code, not a raw String message
CitiesRepository exposes a typed Result/sealed failure for I/O errors instead of letting exceptions reach citySearchProvider raw
A widget test under Locale('he') asserts no raw exception text (e.g. 'Exception:', 'TimeoutException') ever renders
